method: The figure was extracted from the F95 PDF with `pdfimages -png` (an embedded JPEG at 135 ppi); the table's frame was found as the darkest column and row profiles of the image's left part (tools/measure_figure.py, find_frame; given by hand with --frame where a line is too faint for the profile, as the file's notes say); each icon's bounding box was read from the clusters of pixels darker than grey level 200 (components, merged within 2 px) and, where the H or E arrow touches an icon, from an ASCII dump of the region, taking the icon's own outline (a cup's rim and body, a glass's rim and body, a spoon's bowl and handle, a fork's tines and handle, a shaker's rounded box) and leaving the arrow and its label out; the object's position is the centre of that box as a fraction of the frame's inner width and height, scaled to the 110 x 100 table (D-001, D-003). The silverware's orientation was read on the enlarged image (tines, blade and bowl at the top: `up`).

uncertainty.note: One pixel is 0.57 units; icon boxes are good to about 1 px, and the objects an arrow overlaps (the touched object, the E1 and E2 objects) to about 2 px; a spoon's bowl under the H arrow is placed from its handle. The uncertainty was measured on Surround 5 against the chapter 4 screen dump of the same configuration (docs/problems.md 5); the Buridan 1 configuration, printed twice (pp. 129 and 130), agrees with itself to within 1.5 units (docs/problems.md 7).

notes: The H arrow enters the touched spoon's bowl from the upper right; the spoon's box is its bowl (6 px wide, centred on the handle) and handle, 17 px, read on the ASCII dump.

The E1 arrow enters Eliza's lower-left spoon from the lower left and the E2 arrow her lower-right object from the lower right; their boxes were read on the ASCII dumps, the arrows and labels left out.

The configuration is printed twice, as 'Buridan 1 (original program)' [F95 p. 129 (img)] and 'Buridan I (modified program)' [F95 p. 130 (img)], 'identical to the previous one' [F95 p. 131]; this file is digitized from the first figure (PDF page 139, image 22). The second figure (PDF page 140, image 24) was measured too: its frame is 193 x 174 px and every object lies within 1.5 units of this file's position, the fork under the E2 arrow the furthest (docs/problems.md 7). Both result sets use this file (`reported.BURIDAN`).
The two cups on each side stand 2 px apart (Henry's) and 1 px apart (Eliza's); the touched spoon's bowl touches cup2's handle.
review: Reviewed: cup, cup, spoon (H) at the top centre; spoon (E1), glass, glass lower left; cup, cup, fork (E2) lower right [F95 p. 129].
